To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Brightline Pro 6% developer, batch LX2291: please check your bottles today

Hi everyone,

Please read this before you do any more colour, especially if you buy from the Kelvin Trade rep. A lot of us do.

WHAT'S HAPPENED

Kelvin Trade emailed on Sunday to say there was a filling error on one batch of Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L. Batch LX2291 may contain 12% (40 vol) developer in a bottle labelled 6%. It was supplied between 19 October and 5 November. They say other batches and other strengths are fine.

It's not a theoretical problem. On Saturday I had a client with a painful scalp reaction during a bleach retouch, and the bottle was from this batch. On Thursday Aileen had a highlights client whose foils were roasting and the lift went mad. She thought she'd left the heater too close. Same developer, same batch. Lorna, I think you picked up a box off him too, so please check.

HOW TO CHECK YOUR BOTTLES

- The batch code is printed on the BASE OF THE BOTTLE. It is not on the box. The box has no batch on it, so checking the box will tell you nothing.
- Look for LX2291. If it says that, don't use it.
- Check the stock in the back AND any bottle you've already opened in your trolley. Mine was opened that morning, so don't assume an open one is fine.
- If you've decanted developer into another bottle and can't tell where it came from, don't use it.
- If the code is worn off or you can't read it, treat it as suspect and ask me or Aileen to have a look.

WHAT IT DOES

It's double the strength you think you're using, so everything happens faster and hotter.

- Much faster lift. My retouch was near pale yellow at 18 minutes. It normally takes 35 to 40. Don't trust your usual timings.
- More than the usual tingle: burning, stinging, redness on the scalp, hot foils.
- Hair that goes brassy, patchy or over-processed, even if the scalp is fine. Aileen's client was brassy and patchy afterwards.

If you've used developer from the last few weeks and a client mentioned burning or odd results, it might be worth giving them a quick call.

WHAT TO DO WITH AFFECTED BOTTLES

- Stop using them straight away.
- If you or a client had a problem, KEEP THAT BOTTLE. Don't bin it. Put it somewhere safe and label it. It's evidence, and your insurer will probably want it. Take photos and keep your notes.
- Everything else can go back. The rep is in on Tuesday and will take bottles back, or you can take them to the Kelvin Trade depot in Hillington. They've said full credit.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR

- Stop the service and get the colour off straight away with cool running water. No shampoo.
- Wear gloves yourself and don't put creams or anything else on the skin.
- Keep rinsing with plenty of cool or lukewarm water. NHS advice for chemical burns is about an hour of running water. Don't stop after a couple of minutes because it looks better.
- Chemical burns need to be looked at in hospital. Call 999 and follow the call handler's instructions. Don't wait for blistering. If there's any trouble breathing, throat swelling or the client collapses, call 999 immediately.
- Once things are settled, write it up in the incident book at the desk. Put the date, time, product and batch number.
- Keep the bottle.

Kelvin Trade's email says sorry for any inconvenience. It's a bit more than an inconvenience when somebody's got a burnt scalp, so please don't take it lightly. Check your bottles today before your next colour goes on.

If you're not sure about anything, come and find me.

Kirsty
